:JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against SCH 15 3 MVC 5732-2022 Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of Raghavendra S/o Late.Puttaiah in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 02102022 at about 9.45 a.m. when the son of Petitioner No.1 by name Raghavendra was proceeding in a Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11B 5569 near Shekar S/o Marikalegowda land, Averahalli village, Koppa hobli, Maddur Taluk, Mandya District and the said vehicle was driven by one Naveen Kumar K. in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life without observing the traffic rules and regulations and he lost control over the vehicle and the vehicle was turtled down in road side.
As a result, Raghavendra had sustained fatal head injuries and succumbed to the said injuries.

3. Immediately, after the accident, the said Raghavendra was shifted to MIMS Govt., hospital,
Mandya and thereafter SCH 15 4 MVC 5732-2022 Post Mortem was conducted in the hospital and deadbody was handed over to the Petitioners and Petitioners had spent more than Rs.2,00,000/
for transportation, funeral and obsequeis etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of accident, said Raghavendra was hale and healthy and he was working as a Cleaner and Loader and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/ per month.
Due to untimely death of deceased, the Petitioners life become dark and miserable and they put to great financial hardship.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Tata Ace Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11B5569.
Therefore, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
2 5.
In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondents 1 and 2 did not appear before the Tribunal.
Hence, they were placed exparte.

SCH 15 5 MVC 5732-2022 6. Heard. Perused the Petition and materials available on record.
7.

Now the point arises for the determination of this Court are as under : POINTS 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that Raghavendra S/o Late. Puttaiah was died in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 210 2022 at about 9.45 a.m. near Shekar S/o Marikalegowda land,
Averahalli village, Koppa hobli, Maddur Taluk, Mandya District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA 11B5569?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of the deceased?
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
8. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 11 and closed her side evidence.
Since, both Respondents were exparte, there is no Respondents side evidence.

9. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and upon going through the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Affirmative  Point No.2 : In the Affirmative  Point No. 3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Point No. 4 :
As per the Final Order  for the following :
SCH 15 7 MVC 5732-2022  REASONS 10.

Point No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tata Ace Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11B 5569 and in the said accident, Raghavendra had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the said injuries.

Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
3 10.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as P.W.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the petition averments.
In order to support her contention, she has relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.

Ex.P1 and Ex P2 are the the True copies of FIR with Complaint which shows that the Koppa Police have registered the case against the driver of offending Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11B5569 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304A of IPC on the complaint lodged by one Kumara C. S/o Kemppaiah SCH 15 8 MVC 5732-2022 ChikkaKenchegowda.
Ex.P3 is the Spot Mahazar with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn the Mahazar at the spot in the presence of Panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the Inquest Mahazar which was drawn on the dead body of deceased Raghavendra.

Ex.P.5 is the true copy of PM report which shows that as per the opinion of the doctor,
the cause of death is due to head injury sustained.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report which shows that accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.

Ex.P.7 is the true copy of the Chargesheet which shows that after the investigation, the I.O of Koppa Police Station has submitted the Chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC and U/s 194A of IMV Act.
Ex.P8 to 10 are the Aadhar cards of Petitioners and deceased Raghavendra and Ex.P11 is the Ration card.
The Column No.17 of Charge Sheet reads as under:

.

.
   279, 337, 304 ()   194 ()   
  ."
Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
4 11.

The ChargeSheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Chargesheeted the driver of the offending Tata Ace vehicle for the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and the accident caused by him and due to the said accident, the son of the PW1 had succumbed to the injuries.

It is pertinent to note here that in spite of service of notice to the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., Respondent SCH 15 11 MVC 5732-2022 No.1 and the insurer of the offending vehicle i.e., Respondent No.2, they did not appear before the court.
Therefore, there is no rebuttal evidence.
Further, the contents of Exhibits remained uncontroverted.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the said Raghavendra had sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 is in the "Affirmative".

Point No.2 and 3:
12.
Both these Points are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
13. It is stated in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased Raghavendra and Petitioner No.2 is SCH 15 12 MVC 5732-2022 the brother of the deceased Raghavendra.
In order to prove this fact, PW1 has produced Aadhar Cards i.e., ExP8 to 10 and Ration card i.e., Ex P11.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased with the Petitioner No.1 and 2.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 have proved that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Raghavendra and they are dependents on the deceased Raghavendra.
14. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 30 years and his avocation is shown as Cleaner and Loader and earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
But PW.1 has not produced any document for income proof.
Therefore, in the absence of actual income proof, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since, the accident has occurred in the year 2022, the income of the deceased is notionally taken at Rs.15,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of SCH 15 13 MVC 5732-2022 compensation.
15. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Raghavendra as 30 years at the time of the accident.
In this regard, the Petitioners have produced Aadhar card of the deceased Raghavendra which marked at Ex.P.10 wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 21.05.1991.
The accident took place on 02.10.2022.
Hence, the age of the deceased Raghavendra to be taken at 31 years for the purpose of Assessment of compensation.
16. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
5 17.
The deceased has left behind his mother and brother.
SCH 15 14 MVC 5732-2022 Hence, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As this Court has already observed that the Petitioners are the mother and brother of the deceased Raghavendra, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for a sum of Rupees 40,000/ towards loss of consortium and Rupees 15,000/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 15,000/ towards funeral expenses.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION, SCH 15 15 MVC 5732-2022 18.
Petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and she lost her son's love and affection.
Petitioner No.2 is the brother, who lost his brother's love and affection.

Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/
under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
19. The Petitioner might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

VII. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
20.
It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was SCH 15 16 MVC 5732-2022 notionally fixed at Rs.15,500/ p.m.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:
"Quantum fatal accident Principle of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged :
21, contract worker in a company - High Court did not consider future prospects while computing compensation - Whether claimants are entitled to compensation after addition of 40 per cent of income of the deceased towards future prospects "

Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd

sentences.text: Held :  yes.

Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
6 2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :
 SCH 15 17 MVC 5732-2022  "Quantum Fatal accident - Principles  of assessment Future prospects Deceased aged  40 Upholding objections of insurance company  that principle of addition on account of future prospects is not applicable where income of the deceased is determined by guesswork, High Court disallowed the addition of 50 per cent made by the Tribunal for future prospects while computing compensation - Whether addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in absence of proof of income Held: Yes:
there cannot be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork :
executing Court directed to respondent compute entitlement of claimants by adding 40 per cent of income for future prospect and make corresponding deduction towards personal expenses".
SCH 15 18 MVC 5732-2022 The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil)
No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 40% below the age of 40 years".

sentences.text:
In this Petition,
the deceased was aged 31 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,500/ comes to Rs.6,200/.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,700/ p.m.
(Rs.15,500/ + Rs.6,200/ = Rs.21,700/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 16.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that, if the deceased was bachelor,
half of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
SCH 15 19 MVC 5732-2022 21.

After deducting half towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,700/ it comes to Rs.10,850/ (21,700/  10,850/) and multiplier applied is 16, (Rs.10,850/ x 12 =
1,30,200/, Rs.1,30,200/ x 16 = 20,83,200/).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,83,200/ towards loss of dependency.

TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 40,000/
Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
7 2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 15,000/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs.20,83,200/ Total Rs.22,08,200/
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.22,08,200/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from SCH 15 20 MVC 5732-2022 the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

22. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending TATA Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA11B5569.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid from 03.08.2022 to 02.08.2023 which is in force at the time of accident.
Though notice was served to the Respondent No.1 and 2, they did not appear before the Court.
Further the ChargeSheet does not shows that there is no valid insurance policy to the offending vehicle.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 is in the "Affirmative" and Point No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
Point No.4

: From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.22,08,200/ along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,08,200/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the SCH 15 22 MVC 5732-2022 compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount as stated supra with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within 60 days from the date of this award.

Sarojamma vs Ravikumar M.C on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122748942/
8

Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 90% to the Petitioner No.1.
2) 10% to the Petitioner No.2 After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 through Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or SCH 15 23 MVC 5732-2022 Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 is ordered to be paid by way of E payment and after his proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
